title: Cybersecurity basics
examples: What is the difference between a virus and malware?
How often should I really be updating my phone?
Can a simple password really keep me safe online?

explain.say: Today we learn about keeping our digital lives safe online. You will learn about phishing and malware. These are common online dangers.
Phishing is when attackers try to trick you into giving away private information. They often send fake emails or messages. Always check the sender's real email address first.
Malware is a general term for any malicious software designed to damage your device. Viruses and ransomware are types of malware. Never download files from unknown sources.
Keeping software updated is very important for security. Updates often fix known weaknesses that attackers could use. Always install updates when your device prompts you to do so.
In real life, you might receive a text message saying your account is locked. It asks you to click a link right away. This is a phishing attempt, so do not click anything.
A common mistake is using the same password everywhere you log in. If one site gets hacked, all your accounts are at risk. Use a strong, unique password for every service.

faq.q: What is the difference between malware and a virus?
faq.a: A virus is a type of malware, but malware is the bigger term. Malware covers all harmful software, while a virus specifically tries to attach itself to other programs.
asks: What is the difference between a virus and malware?

faq.q: If I get a suspicious email, should I delete it right away?
faq.a: It is safer to report it first if you can. If you are sure it is dangerous, then deleting it is a good final step. Do not interact with it in any way.
asks: Should I open it to check?
What should I do with a suspicious email?

faq.q: Do I have to update everything on my phone all the time?
faq.a: Yes, keeping your operating system updated is crucial for security. These updates often patch security holes that criminals look for. It is like fixing a broken lock on your digital door.
asks: How often do I need to update my phone?

faq.q: What makes a password strong enough to be safe?
faq.a: A strong password uses a mix of upper and lower case letters, numbers, and symbols. It should also be long enough that it cannot be guessed easily. Think of a memorable phrase.
asks: How long should my password be?

faq.q: Can I trust links sent by friends on social media?
faq.a: Sometimes even friends' accounts can be hacked. Always be suspicious of unexpected links, even if they seem to come from someone you know. Ask them another way to confirm.
asks: How do I know if a friend's account is hacked?

facts: Phishing attempts often create a sense of urgency to make you act quickly.
Malware can steal personal data like passwords and credit card numbers.
Software updates contain 'patches' that fix security vulnerabilities.
Using a unique password for every account adds a major layer of protection.

quiz.say: You receive an email from your 'bank' asking you to click a link to verify your password immediately.
quiz.show: What is this email most likely to be?
quiz.why: Phishing emails create false emergencies to trick you into giving away private details.

wrong.0: Real banks usually ask you to log in through their official app, not via an email link.
wrong.1: Updates are for your device software, not for your bank account details.
wrong.3: Malware is the harmful program itself, not the email trick.

quiz.say: If you download a file from a website you have never heard of, what risk are you taking?
quiz.why: Unknown files could contain malware that damages your device without you knowing it.

wrong.0: The danger is software, not just speed.
wrong.1: The risk can be serious, including losing all your data.
wrong.3: It is never safe to download from unknown sources.

quiz.say: When setting up a new online account, what is the best practice for your password?

options.show: Use your pet's name and birthday
options.say: Use your pet's name and birthday

quiz.why: A unique passphrase is hard to guess and cannot be used if another site is hacked.

wrong.0: Reusing passwords means one breach compromises everything.
wrong.1: Short passwords are easily broken by simple guessing programs.
wrong.3: Personal information is very easy for attackers to guess.
